title: Teachers can see the five newer games in the class grid and Today alerts
wrong: Teachers cannot see Pigeon, Parrot, Lizard, Swamp Hen or Robin in the class grid or Today alerts.
done: Each of the five has a column set in the class grid and its alerts show on the Today page.
why: A teacher can only help children who are stuck if the stuck children show up.

title: Small fixes found in play in Lizard, Pigeon, Robin and Swamp Hen
wrong: A raft tip on a go with no raft, a dot called an arrow, Robin help off the screen and overlapping berries, and Swamp Hen cards that give the answer away by shape.
done: Play each game and none of these show: help is in view, berries do not overlap, and the four cards look alike.
why: Clear help and fair choices mean the child is thinking about the maths, not the screen.

title: Help for each kind of go in the newer five games
wrong: Each game keeps one help level for the whole child, so a strong kind of go and a weak kind get the same help.
done: Help fades on a kind the child does well and stays on a kind they find hard.
why: Help that fits each kind of go keeps hard things supported without over-helping easy ones.

title: Review Kingfisher's Dairy once it is live
wrong: Kingfisher's Dairy has not been scored by the blind review like the other games.
done: It has a blind score, a row on the review page and a fix card for each real problem.
why: The newest game gets the same check as the rest before more children use it.
